implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded 'Hero Video' block (componentId: component-001, canonicalBlockName: hero-video, selector: div.herovideo) sourced directly from https://www.disneycampus.com/. The live page confirms the block renders as div.herovideo with class 'block', height 438.75px at y:64 (immediately below the 64px header), full viewport width 780px. The authored table has a single data row with four cells: [video asset], [heading: DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED], [primary CTA link: PLAY FULL VIDEO], [secondary CTA link: LEARN MORE]. Section metadata for the containing section provides subtitles, poster, and transcript as configurable assets — these are NOT block cells but section-metadata rows and must be handled via the section-metadata block, not hardcoded. The block does not exist in the repository (inventory shows: cards, columns, footer, fragment, header, hero, widget — no herovideo). The canonical block name from the live site stylesheet is 'herovideo' (https://www.disneycampus.com/blocks/herovideo/herovideo.css is loaded), matching the div.herovideo selector. The story acceptance criteria require: exact text content rendered (Video label, playback helper text, heading, two CTAs), one configurable video media area, no hardcoded unavailable values, keyboard operation for video (Enter/Space), and accessible names on both CTAs. The block JS must: (1) read the four authored cells — video link/asset, heading, primary CTA, secondary CTA; (2) build a <video> element with keyboard play/pause via keydown Enter/Space; (3) expose aria-label on both CTA anchors matching their visible text; (4) render a visible 'Video' label and the playback helper text 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' as authored. The section-metadata (subtitles, poster, transcript) is already handled by the EDS section-metadata block and will be available as data attributes or section properties — the herovideo block JS should read poster and subtitles from the section's dataset if present, keeping them configurable. Typography (InspireTWDCBlack, font-weight:900, font-size:24px for CTAs; heading styles) and colors (white text on video overlay) are observed from computed styles but must not be hardcoded as magic values — they must use CSS custom properties scoped to the block. The PLAY FULL VIDEO link has aria-label 'PLAY FULL VIDEO about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and href '#fullscreen-cta' in the live page; LEARN MORE has aria-label 'LEARN MORE about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and href '/about'. These destinations are configurable per acceptance criteria. The block CSS must be mobile-first, use CSS custom properties for all visual tokens, and not hardcode pixel spacing or color values that were marked uncaptured.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) authoritatively maps the Program categories section to a 'Cards (overlay)' block — canonicalBlockName 'cards', authoredLabel 'Cards (overlay)', selector 'div.cards.overlay'. The authored table structure is a two-column collection: each row contains [image cell, label cell, link cell] but the nested-object placeholders in the contract rows indicate the image and link cells were captured from the live site. The planning story requires exactly four category items (PERFORMING ARTS, ARTS & HUMANITIES, SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY, LEADERSHIP & INNOVATION) rendered as interactive link-like items with configurable destinations. The repository already contains blocks/cards/cards.js and blocks/cards/cards.css (boilerplate implementation). The live site evidence confirms the rendered block carries classes 'cards overlay block size-4 clickable overlay-animation' on a <div>, with an inner <ul> rendered as a CSS grid (grid-template-columns: 780px; grid-template-rows: 546px 546px 546px 546px at mobile, 20px gap). The sourceText from the Content Agent confirms two rows were captured with links to https://main--disneycampus--twdc-minnie.aem.live/programs/performing-arts and /programs/arts-humanities — these are internal AEM preview URLs, not the final destination URLs, confirming the planning requirement that link targets must remain configurable. The 'overlay' variant is the discriminating class that distinguishes this from the generic cards block. The existing boilerplate cards.js/cards.css do not implement the overlay variant at all — they implement a generic image+body card grid. Therefore the correct scope is to ADD the overlay variant CSS and JS decoration logic to the existing cards block files, not create a new block. This is the smallest safe repository scope: modify blocks/cards/cards.js to handle the overlay variant (text-only cards with link wrapping, no image required per the category-links use case) and add blocks/cards/cards.css overlay variant rules. The four category labels contain HTML entities (& for &) which must be rendered correctly and exposed as accessible names matching the visible text including literal ampersands. No images, descriptions, or additional media are present in the captured evidence for this specific overlay/category-links variant — the acceptance criteria explicitly forbid introducing media not present in evidence. The block table structure from the Content Agent has rows with three cells each (image placeholder, label, link placeholder); the JS decorator must handle the case where the image cell is empty or absent for the overlay variant, wrapping the entire card in an anchor derived from the link cell.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The repository already contains blocks/header/header.js and blocks/header/header.css (boilerplate EDS header). The Content Agent document does NOT include a header block table — the header is a global shared pattern loaded via loadHeader() in scripts.js from a /nav fragment path. This is the canonical EDS header pattern: the block reads a /nav document fragment and decorates it into brand, sections, and tools nav areas. The planning story requires: (1) contact bar with 'Questions?', 'Call (321) 939 7560', and 'Contact Us' link; (2) primary nav labels ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, CONNECT WITH US; (3) logo/brand link; (4) search control; (5) configurable link destinations; (6) header landmark + keyboard accessibility. The live site evidence confirms: header-wrapper at y=0, height=64px, z-index=1000; nav#nav with display:flex, border-bottom:1px solid rgb(0,0,0), max-width:1140px, padding:0 12px; nav-wrapper with z-index:600, background-color:rgb(255,255,255); the header block text includes 'Skip to main content Questions? Call (321) 939 7560 Contact Us About Us … Curriculum & Tickets … Special Events … Plan Your Trip … Connect With Us' confirming all required content is present in the rendered header. The existing header.js loads a /nav fragment and maps children[0]=brand, children[1]=sections, children[2]=tools. The /nav document must be authored with: row 0 = brand (logo link), row 1 = nav sections list, row 2 = tools (contact bar + search). The implementation must extend header.js to handle the contact bar (Questions? + phone + Contact Us link) and search control within the tools area, and extend header.css to style these areas without hardcoding uncaptured color tokens, typography, or spacing values — using CSS custom properties instead. The nav-height CSS variable is already defined as 64px in styles.css matching the observed 64px header height. No new block is needed; the existing header block is modified to support the Disney Imagination Campus nav document structure. Content gap: the Content Agent document contains no header/nav block table — this is expected because the header is a global pattern loaded from a /nav fragment, not a page-body block. The /nav document authoring model is documented in the filePlan as a content model note for the Content Agent.

visualSummary.responsiveBehavior: At 780px viewport (observed): header height 64px, nav is flex row with hamburger visible. At ≥900px (boilerplate breakpoint): nav-wrapper position changes from fixed to relative, nav switches to flex justify-content:space-between, hamburger hidden, sections visible. The contact/tools area must be visible on desktop inline with brand and sections.
